description:
## Goal

The public compiler2 trace allowlist must advertise only signals that can actually be emitted.

## Current defect

At main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, `is_public_compiler2_trace_event` still accepts three event families with no emitter anywhere in Rust source:

- `["fz", "compiler2", "work", "started"]`
- `["fz", "compiler2", "pull", "phase", ..]`
- `["fz", "compiler2", "drive", "stalled"]`

Each terminal literal (`started`, `phase`, `stalled`) occurs only in that allowlist. A public row therefore falsely advertises a signal that cannot appear.

## Later-main correction already present

fz-kdt.34 added and tested the live `["fz", "compiler2", "drive", "demand_on_stall"]` signal, including its JSONL projection and exact demanded-fact/reason payload. `drive.stalled` is not needed as an alias. Work-start information is reported by `pull.session.finished`; current pull telemetry uses session/product events, not a `pull.phase.*` family.

## Strategy

Delete the three dead allowlist alternatives. Do not invent compatibility emitters for names with no current contract. Add a source-inventory regression that fails when a compiler2 public allowlist row/family has neither a production emitter nor an explicit sink-born exception such as `canon.*`.

## TDD / acceptance

- First add the inventory regression and show it reports exactly the three dead rows.
- Remove the rows and show the regression passes.
- Every public compiler2 allowlist row/family is backed by a production emitter, except documented sink-born `canon.*`.
- `drive.demand_on_stall` remains public and its focused trace test passes.
- Relevant docs do not advertise deleted names.
- Full tests, formatting, and strict clippy pass.
title: Three public-trace allowlist rows have no emitter anywhere in the tree
